messages:
maria: heads-up — onboarding Jupiter-13B (float->int8) is hitting OOMs on coldstart in canary. started at 08:12 UTC, reproduces ~60-70% of the time on node-type g4dn-xlarge.
kai: any logs yet? stack traces?
maria: pasted the core error here from the canary pod log:
```
2024-06-20T08:12:03Z ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
Model: jupiter-13b-int8, batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=2048
Allocating KV cache for seq_len=4096 tokens triggered allocation spike
```
sam: batch_size=4 seems high for a cold start on that instance. int8 reduces model weights but KV and intermediate scratch still large.
olivia: +1. default max_new_tokens=2048 is risky for long-run decoding when user prompts are long. We need a safer default for new models.
tj: quick repro notes: if we set `batch_size=1` and `max_new_tokens=512` the pod finishes warmup with ~1.2GB free margin. with batch=4 it immediately OOMs during first step.
maria: is this fragmentation or a single huge allocation? logs show many small cudaMalloc attempts then one big fail.
kai: likely mixed. int8 kernels sometimes allocate temporary float buffers for fused ops. on first decode we hit simultaneous allocations: weights + temp tensors + KV reserve.
infra-bot: traced allocation timeline -> see dashboard: https://infradash/team/jupiter-13b/canary-2024-06-20 (heatmap attached in console)
sam: thought: can we kick off a warmup sequence that forces KV pre-allocation to spread allocations over time? e.g. two-phase warmup: small prompt then a longer prompt after GC window.
olivia: we tried naive warmup before, but allocator fragmentation remained. Suggestion: reduce `max_new_tokens` default for this model family to 512 and set `warmup_steps=3` with `batch_target=1` for first 30s.
tj: patch proposal (quick):
```yaml
model_defaults:
  jupiter-13b-int8:
    max_new_tokens: "512"
    default_batch_size: "1"
    warmup_prompts: ["Hello", "Please summarize:"]
    kv_prefetch: "disabled"
```
maria: disabling kv_prefetch is ok as a mitigation but it will regress latency for medium prompts. prioritize memory safety first.
kai: another lever — enable delayed temp-buffer allocation (lazy-fused-kernel flag) in runtime for int8 paths. This defers some scratch until after KV is reserved.
sam: does runtime support that flag in stable? might be behind feature flag in canary only.
kai: canary-only for now. we can toggle for the Jupiter onboard rollout.
olivia: also noticed some callers send very long system prompts. we should add a server-side hard cap enforcement and return a 400 if prompt+max_new_tokens > 4096 by default.
tj: agree. quick mitigation list: 1) set conservative defaults (max_new_tokens=512, batch=1), 2) disable kv_prefetch for canary, 3) enable lazy-temp flag in runtime canary, 4) add prompt-length enforcement in frontdoor.
maria: assigning actions — @kai takes runtime flag, @sam adjusts model defaults and frontdoor cap, @olivia coordinates canary rollout and monitors latency tradeoffs. I'll add a short eval to see quality diff at 512 vs 2048 for our task set.
kai: started branch: runtime/feat/lazy-temp-int8, will link PR when ready.
sam: updated model config in staging and pushed canary with batch=1, max_new_tokens=512. canary logs now show successful warmup most runs.
infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary deployment 1739130120 -> success (3/4 pods healthy), rollout paused for observation.
deploy-bot: scheduled auto-rollback if OOM rate > 5% in 15m window.
olivia: monitoring dashboards: memory peak stable, but p95 latency increased ~8% due to kv_prefetch off. keeping that tradeoff for now.
tj: remaining followups: long-term we want kernel-level fusion that avoids temp buffers + better allocator defragmentation. file follow-up: ENG-ML-1729.
maria: thanks team — will post a short doc in /docs/onboard/jupiter-13b with the recommended defaults and the canary notes. ping me if you see regressions. :thumbsup:
